state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were trying to make a physical model of this shape using paper — would your net be able to fold into the shape you're thinking of?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess if I tried to fold the net into a triangle, it wouldn't really work because it doesn't have straight edges like a triangle does. But I'm still not sure what shape it actually makes. Is it something like a cone or a cylinder?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were trying to wrap a piece of paper around this shape to see what it looks like from all angles — would your net still make sense in 3D space?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively engages the misconception through visualization prompts that require reasoning, but when the student narrows it down to cone or cylinder in Turn 2, the teacher repeats a similar vague prompt instead of providing targeted scaffolding to help distinguish between these options, leaving the student still uncertain at the end.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, physical analogies (folding paper, wrapping paper around shapes) to help the student visualize and understand the abstract geometric concept of nets and 3D shapes.
